meaning: Carcharhinus, from Greek karcharias “a kind of shark” (from karcharos “saw-like, jagged”, for its teeth) + rhinus, an ancient word for sharks; obscurus, Latin for “dark”, probably referring to its darkish blue-gray body colour
description: A large, slender grey shark with a short, rounded snout, long sickle-shaped pectoral fins and a low ridge between the two dorsal fins. It is bronzy to blue-grey above and white below, with fin tips that darken, especially in young sharks. It grows slowly, maturing only at around 20 years of age, and eats mostly fish, other sharks and rays, and squid.
eats: Bony fish, sharks, rays and squid
